text: A stable $\infty$-category is characterized by which property?
choices: Every inner horn has a unique filler
All morphisms are invertible at every level
The suspension and loop functors are inverse equivalences
Colimits distribute over products and descent holds
explanation: The chapter defines a stable $\infty$-category as one in which suspension and loop are inverse equivalences, generalizing triangulated categories (examples: spectra $\mathrm{Sp}$, derived categories $\mathcal{D}(R)$). 'All morphisms invertible' describes an $\infty$-groupoid; 'colimits distribute over products / descent' are the Giraud-style axioms for an $\infty$-topos; and unique horn fillers describe the nerve of an ordinary category.
